title: Father's remarriage and living with grandparents in Portland
summary: His father remarries around 1920 and builds a house nearby, but Leeman stays with his grandparents and goes through Portland schools.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: What other musical background did you have? You tell me about your music background and your schooling, your young days. Now you were with your grandparents, where we are right now, before we got to Harry Bower -- you were with your grandparents, and you had a half-sister, is that right?
That's later on. My father got married in 1920 -- I just went through the family Bible. He remarried in '20 and '21.
Well, were you living with him then?
No, I was still living with my grandparents, but it was an unusual setup because all this time, my father's business was going on, and my grandfather's was going on.

And he finally -- we bought a farm which was only 4 or 5 miles from Portland, Maine, and my father built a house there. He was doing fairly well, and he was so close -- I was only 10 minutes away, but it seemed to be convenient at the time, with another new marriage, and I continued my schooling in the heart of Portland -- I went
through all the grade schools there and through Portland High School. So convenience sake, rather than live with my father, I lived with my grandfolks.
And it seemed to be a convenient way all around, except I don't want to get into childhood ...
I was a very fortunate person.

Well, we should because this is the history of your life -- don't you think we should get into your childhood? I think maybe the young people might like to know how you came about -- if there were mistakes, if there were misfortunes, perhaps we can sidestep them.
